_README: Earnings announcement dates, maintained by hand.
Format: {SYMBOL: [ISO dates]}, newest first. Include PAST dates too --
they are what a historical-move comparison would be built from later.
A symbol with an empty list simply gets no earnings flag. That is a
known gap, not a claim that no earnings are coming, and the UI says so
rather than implying the name is clean.
Deliberately hand-maintained: 24 symbols x 4 dates a year is a few
minutes a quarter, against a scraped feed that breaks silently and sits
in a terms-of-service grey area. Accuracy here matters more than
convenience -- a wrong date mislabels which expiry carries the event.
Fill from any investor-relations page or earnings calendar. Use the
announcement DATE; whether it is before or after the close does not
change which expiry contains it for the weeklies this tracks.
_provenance: Seeded 2026-10-22 from Nasdaq's published earnings-date pages
THESE ARE EXPECTED DATES, NOT CONFIRMED ONES. Nasdaq's own wording is
'expected* to report'. Companies move them, sometimes by a week, and a
shifted date mislabels which expiry carries the event. Treat the flag
as a prompt to check, not as an authority, and correct from the
company's investor-relations page when it matters to a position.
17 of 19 were corroborated against the options market at the time of
seeding: the implied-vol kink in the term structure lined up with the
claimed date (see src/dashboard/event_vol.py). The two that did not:
AAPL  1.2% implied -- low, though AAPL genuinely has small earnings
moves, so this may be correct rather than a wrong date.
SPCX  no event priced at all. Worth verifying before relying on it.
No dates available for MU, JPM, NFLX, APLD -- Nasdaq's vendor had none.
SPX is an index and has no earnings; its empty list is correct forever.
Only NEXT dates were available from this source. Past dates still need
adding by hand before any historical-move comparison is possible.
